links.outcome: Model performance validated across multiple international sites and uncurated clinical datasets versus prior model
links.effect: On a 555-patient multi-institutional, international test cohort, SIGNAL achieved 90.10% overall accuracy vs 72.59% for DeepGlioma, which had been validated on curated images.
links.quote: SIGNAL outperformed DeepGlioma, achieving greater overall accuracy (90.10% vs. 72.59%) while running faster (16.0 vs. 6.7 patches/s).

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate AI against prior model on the same data
links.effect: SIGNAL outperformed DeepGlioma on IDH mutation (93.51% vs. 79.22%), 1p19q codeletion (93.51% vs. 88.31%), and ATRX loss (89.61% vs. 83.98%).
links.quote: SIGNAL also outperformed DeepGlioma on all three molecular classification tasks, including IDH mutation (accuracy: 93.51% vs. 79.22%), 1p19q codeletion (93.51% vs. 88.31%), and ATRX loss (89.61% vs. 83.98%).

links.outcome: Attention-based rejection of uninformative images (blood, acellular regions) before classification, versus model without rejection
links.effect: DeepGlioma without image rejection underperformed on uncurated data (72.59% accuracy); SIGNAL with attention filtering reached 90.10%. Attention correlated with cellularity (r=0.96) and negatively with blood coverage (r=-0.99).
links.quote: SIGNAL’s attention mechanism had a strong positive linear correlation with mean patch cellularity (r=0.96, p<0.001) and a strong negative correlation with patch blood coverage (r=-0.99,p<0.001).

unlisted_practices: Built-in attention-based image quality rejection filter for intraoperative imaging AI
Lightweight model design for faster intraoperative inference on existing hardware

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic performance and speed of a new lightweight model (SIGNAL) with a built-in attention-based quality filter/image rejection mechanism on real-world uncurated clinical data across multiple international centers, specifically testing the safeguard of filtering diagnostically uninformative tissue.
